verses.1: Having heard that great roar, Lord Yama considered the enemy victorious and his own army destroyed.
verses.2: Indeed, he (Yama), considering his warriors killed and his eyes reddened with anger, quickly told his charioteer, "Bring this chariot near."
verses.3: Then, his charioteer, having brought near the divine great chariot, stood ready, and Yama, of great splendor, indeed ascended that chariot, while Death, holding a spear and mace, stood before him.
verses.4: The imperishable three worlds are brought to an end by him, and the staff of Time, Yama's divine, blazing, fiery weapon, appeared personified by his side.
verses.5: On his sides were placed the inescapable nooses of Time.
verses.6: An embodied mace, whose touch was like fire, also stood there.
verses.7: Then, having seen Time thus enraged and terrifying to all worlds, the three worlds were agitated and the gods trembled.
verses.8: Then, the charioteer, urging those brightly shining horses, proceeded with a terrible roar to where the lord of Rakshasas was situated.
verses.9: In an instant, those horses, swift as thought and resembling Indra's steeds, brought Yama to the place where the battle had begun.
verses.10: Upon seeing that terrifying chariot, which seemed to embody death itself, the ministers of Ravana immediately fled in every direction.
verses.11: Overwhelmed by fear and having lost their senses due to their weak courage, they declared, "We are not capable of fighting here," and fled in all directions.
verses.12: But Ravana, upon seeing that chariot which struck terror into the world, was neither disturbed nor did fear enter his heart.
verses.13: Yama, greatly enraged, approached Ravana and hurled spears and javelins, piercing Ravana's vital spots.
verses.14: Ravana, having regained his composure, then released a shower of arrows upon Yama's chariot, much like a cloud pouring down rain.
verses.15: Then, as powerful arrows struck his broad chest, that demon, afflicted by the shafts, was unable to retaliate.
verses.16: Thus, for seven nights in battle, the enemy Ravana was rendered senseless and turned away by Yama, the tormentor of foes, using various weapons.
verses.17: Then, a fierce battle ensued between Yama and the demon, both unyielding warriors desiring victory in their fight.
verses.18: Then, the gods, along with Gandharvas, Siddhas, and great sages, assembled at that battlefield, led by Prajapati Brahma.
verses.19: Then, the battle between the chief of the Rākṣasas and the lord of the departed spirits became like the cosmic dissolution of the worlds.
verses.20: The lord of Rākṣasas, drawing his bow which shone like Indra's thunderbolt, then released arrows, making the sky appear as if it had no gaps.
verses.21: Rāvaṇa wounded Death with four sharp arrows, afflicted the charioteer with seven, and quickly struck Yama in his vital spots with a hundred thousand arrows.
verses.22: Then, from the enraged Yama's face, a fire of anger arose, garlanded with flames, accompanied by his breath and smoke.
verses.23: Then, having witnessed that marvel in the presence of gods and Dānavas, Death and Kāla became greatly delighted and exceedingly furious.
verses.24: Then, Death, even more enraged, spoke to Yama, saying, "Release me in battle so that I may kill this sinful demon, for by nature, this demon should not exist today as a boundary."
verses.25: The glorious Hiranyakashipu, Namuchi, Shambara, Visandhi, Dhumaketu, and Bali Vairochana were among them.
verses.26: Dambhu, the great king of Daityas, Vritra, and Bana, along with royal sages who knew the scriptures, Gandharvas, and great serpents, were also present.
verses.27: Sages, serpents, Daityas, Yakshas, and groups of Apsaras, along with the earth and its great oceans at the end of an age, were all present.
verses.28: O great king, these and many other powerful and formidable beings, along with mountains, rivers, and trees, were all brought to destruction.
verses.29: I have seen many fallen, so what to say of this demon?
verses.30: O knower of dharma, release me so I may kill this one, for no one seen by me, however powerful, has ever lived.
verses.31: This is not merely my strength, but a natural rule that anyone seen by me does not live even for a moment.
verses.32: Having heard his words, the powerful Dharmaraja then said to Death, "You wait, I will kill this one."
verses.33: Then, the enraged Lord Yama, with blood-red eyes, indeed lifted his unfailing rod of death with his hand.
verses.34: On whose sides all the nooses of Death are established, and an embodied mace, resembling fire and lightning, stands.
verses.35: What more can be said of one who is touched or struck down, when merely by sight it draws away the lives of living beings?
verses.36: That great weapon, surrounded by flames as if burning the demon, trembled when touched by the powerful Yama.
verses.37: Then all those on the battlefield, terrified by that, fled, and all the gods were agitated upon seeing Yama with his mace raised.
verses.38: When Yama was indeed desirous of striking Ravana with his mace, the grandfather Brahma directly appeared before Yama and spoke these words.
verses.39: O mighty-armed Yama, son of Vivasvat, you of immeasurable prowess, indeed that demon should not be killed by your staff alone.
verses.40: O chief among gods, indeed a boon has been given by me to him, and that word spoken by me should not be made false by you.
verses.41: Whoever, be it a god or even a human, would make my word false, by him the three worlds would indeed be made false, there is no doubt about this.
verses.42: This terrible staff, when released by an angry one, destroys creatures without distinction between dear and not dear, causing fear to all three worlds.
verses.43: Indeed, this unfailing staff of Time, of immeasurable power for all living beings, was created by me long ago, with Death as its foremost aspect.
verses.44: O gentle one (Yama), this rod of yours should certainly not be cast upon Ravana's head, for indeed, no one survives even for a moment once this rod has fallen.
verses.45: If this demon (Ravana) does not die even after this rod has fallen, or if Ravana dies, then in either case, it would be a falsehood (regarding the boon of immortality).
verses.46: Therefore, withdraw this uplifted rod from Ravana and make my words true now, if you indeed care for the worlds.
verses.47: Thus spoken to, the righteous Yama then replied, "This rod has been withdrawn, for indeed, you are our powerful lord."
verses.48: What indeed can I do now, having come to battle, if this one (Ravana) cannot be killed by me because he is protected by a boon?
verses.49: Having said, "Therefore, I disappear from the sight of this demon," he vanished right there with his chariot and horses.
verses.50: Dashagriva, having conquered him and proclaimed his own name, ascended the Pushpaka chariot again and departed from Yama's abode.
